title: Explicit coefficient comparison at the proper/open junction
statement: Fix a finite-field datum \(D\), its coefficient datum \(C\), a finite extension \(E\) of \(\mathbb Q_\ell\), an integer \(n\ge1\), and a normalized six-functor operation datum \(S\) at \((E,n)\). Assume \(\ell\) is invertible in \(D.k\). Let \(o\) be the simultaneous-system operations and \(z\) their specified realization data. Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a quasi-compact morphism of six-functor spaces and \(c=(j:X\to\bar X,p:\bar X\to Y)\) a compactification of its underlying scheme morphism. Set \(A=S.\mathrm{higher}.\mathrm{integralExchange}(\mathrm{identitySquare}(f,c))\). Use the integral object categories, reduction functors and coordinate maps of [def-sf-integral-projection-coordinate-data]. The proper pull comparison is reduction of the specified proper-pull equality followed by pullValue and pullReduction. Define directReduction on an integral constructible object \(M\) on \(\bar X\) by transposing the inverse proper pull comparison followed by reduction of the actual proper counit under the system proper adjunction. Define openReduction on an integral constructible object \(K\) on \(X\) by reduction of the datum's ordinary open realization followed by the inverse whole-system open reduction mate; [lem-sf-open-reconstruction-effectivity] and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] supply its invertibility. For integral constructible \(K\) on \(X\) and \(L\) on \(Y\), define middleMap from reduction of \(A.\mathrm{properPush}(T_{\bar X}(A.\mathrm{openExtension}(K),A.\mathrm{properPull}(L)))\) to \(p_*T_{\bar X}(j_!\mathrm{red}(K),p^*\mathrm{red}(L))\) by directReduction followed by proper image of tensor reduction and these open/pull comparisons. Define systemFirst as the actual proper projection mate with its uncurried source and target written explicitly. Define systemSecond as proper image of the system open projection followed by the inverse pullback compositor and compactification equation. These are explicit composites; neither projection nor an existential coordinate choice defines middleMap.
